- `src/catering/catering-states.mjs:35` (import at `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:10`): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 1 (named exports only, default exports forbidden). `advanceOrder` is exported as `export default advanceOrder;`, and the service imports it as a default import (`import advanceOrder, {canAmend, canCancel, newOrder} from './catering-states.mjs'`). Fix: change to a named export (for example `export const advanceOrder = ...`) and import it by name in `catering-service.mjs`.

- `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:54`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.1 and 6.2. The rule module `vendorNotice` reads the clock with `sentAt: Date.now()`. Only service modules may read the current time, and rule modules must receive instants as parameters. Fix: have `vendorNotice(order, menu, sentAt)` receive the instant as a number, and have `notifyVendor` in `src/catering/catering-service.mjs` (which is called from `placeOrder` with the single `at = now()` value) pass `at` through.

- `src/catering/catering-pricing.mjs:35`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.2. `cancellationFee(order, context)` is a rule module export that receives the whole `context` object and calls `context.now()`. Rule modules must receive instants (numbers), never a `now` function. Fix: change the signature to `cancellationFee(order, at)`, and have `cancelOrder` pass the instant it already read.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:109-112` (with `src/catering/catering-pricing.mjs:35`): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.3 (a service function calls `now` at most once per call). `cancelOrder` calls `now()` in `advanceOrder(order, 'cancel', now())`, and `cancellationFee` calls `context.now()` again, so one cancellation reads the clock twice. Near the `cancelCutoff` boundary, `canceledAt` and the fee decision can use different instants, so the record can be inconsistent. Fix: read `const at = now();` once in `cancelOrder` and pass `at` to both `advanceOrder` and the fee calculation.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:124-126` (helper `isUpcoming` at line 122): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 6.3. `upcomingOrders` passes `now` into `isUpcoming`, which calls `now()` once per order inside `.filter`. A single listing therefore reads the clock N times and may compare orders against different instants. Fix: `export const upcomingOrders = async ({memberId, now, store}) => { const at = now(); ... }` and make the predicate take `at` as a number (`order.deliverAt >= at`).

- `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:1`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 2 (only store and platform modules may import Node.js built-in modules). `kitchen-manifest.mjs` is a rule module (its name is neither `*-service.mjs` nor `*-store.mjs`), yet it imports `createHash` from `node:crypto` to compute the manifest digest. Fix: move the digest computation into a platform module (for example a `src/platform/` helper that hashes a string) and have the rule module call that helper, or have the service compute the digest.

- `src/catering/menu.mjs:11`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 3. `export const DIETARY_TAGS = Object.keys(DIETARY_LABELS);` exports an array that is not frozen. Fix: `export const DIETARY_TAGS = Object.freeze(Object.keys(DIETARY_LABELS));`.

- `src/catering/menu.mjs:35-42` (`loadMenu`): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.1. A rule module must not catch errors, but `loadMenu` wraps `JSON.parse` in `try`/`catch` and rethrows a new error. `menuFor` in `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:16-22` already wraps any failure from `loadMenu` with `{cause: error}`, so the catch in `loadMenu` is redundant and the error context is preserved without it. Fix: remove the `try`/`catch` from `loadMenu` and let `JSON.parse` throw; the service keeps the single place where the error is translated.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:35`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.2. `notifyVendor` replaces the caught error with `new Error(message, error)`, passing the caught error as the second argument rather than as `cause`. The original error is therefore not preserved as `cause`. Fix: `throw new Error(\`vendor of order ${order.id} was not notified\`, {cause: error});`.

- `src/catering/catering-store.mjs:33-41` (`save`, catch at line 39): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 4.3. A store may catch only to keep its write queue usable, but the promise returned to the caller must still reject with the original error. The chain ends with `.catch(() => undefined)` and the same promise is returned, so a failed write (for example the duplicate `requestKey` check at `requestKeyHolder`) resolves to `undefined` and the original error is lost. Concrete consequence: `saveThenNotify` in `src/platform/records.mjs` (`const saved = await store.save(record); await send(saved);`) then calls `notifier.placed(placedNotice(undefined, menu))`, which throws a `TypeError` instead of reporting "request key is already used by order ...". Fix: keep the queue alive with a separate chain, for example `const write = this.#writes.then(() => {...}); this.#writes = write.catch(() => undefined); return write;`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:70-75` (`addLine`): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5 (exported functions must not mutate caller-supplied objects or arrays; records returned by an injected store count as caller-supplied). `amended = {...order}` is a shallow copy, so `amended.lines` is the same array as `order.lines`, and `amended.lines.push(prepareLine(line))` mutates the caller's order before validation. If `itemsFor` then throws (menu item not offered or not meeting dietary needs), the caller's order already contains an extra line that was never saved. Fix: build a new array, for example `const amended = {...order, lines: [...order.lines, prepareLine(line)]};`, then validate and compute the charge from `amended`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:89-96` (`postponeOrder`): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5. `Object.assign(order, {deliverAt, postponedAt: now()})` mutates the record returned by `store.find`. For the in-memory store that is the same object held in the store, so when `checkDeliverySlot` then throws (front desk closed, outside reservation, or room clash), the stored order keeps the new `deliverAt` even though the postponement failed. Fix: `const postponed = {...order, deliverAt, postponedAt: at};` after reading `at = now()` once, run `checkDeliverySlot` on `postponed`, and `return store.save(postponed);`.

- `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:27` (`inDeliveryOrder`, used at line 51): Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 5. `orders.sort(byDelivery)` sorts the caller-supplied `orders` array in place, and the exported `kitchenManifests` relies on it. The helper name `inDeliveryOrder` also does not reveal that it mutates its argument (Mysterious Name). It is also a Middle Man: it adds no policy beyond the sort. Fix: delete `inDeliveryOrder` and write `orders.filter((order) => order.state === 'confirmed' && contains(period, deliveryWindow(order))).sort(byDelivery)`, so only the new filtered array is sorted.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:4`: Violates `src/AGENTS.md` rule 7.2. A feature module may import only rule modules of another feature, never service or store modules. `isFrontDeskOpen` is exported from `src/schedules/front-desk-service.mjs`, a service module of the `schedules` feature. Fix: move the open-check capability to a location the catering feature may use. `src/schedules/desk-policy.mjs` already exports the pure `isDeskOpen(schedule, closures, at)`, so the schedules feature could expose a rule-level function that takes the loaded schedule and closures, with the load kept in the schedules service. Alternatively, follow rule 7.4 and move the capability to a platform module.

- `src/catering/catering-store.mjs:12`: Violates the Source Checkout JavaScript style in `docs/agents/writing.md` (Repository-owned section): "除非外部 Interface 要求, 否则避免使用 `class`" (avoid `class` unless an external interface requires it). Nothing in this change requires a class: the sibling store `src/billing/invoice-store.mjs` implements the same behavior (Map state, write queue, `Object.freeze` interface) with a factory closure. Fix: rewrite `CateringStore` as `createCateringStore`, returning `Object.freeze({find, findByRequestKey, list, save})` over closure-held `records` and `writes` variables, matching `createInvoiceStore`.

- `src/catering/menu.mjs:52` (used at `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:2,10`): Violates `docs/agents/writing.md` Common capabilities ("不得创建只转发调用且没有隐藏任何复杂性的公共包装器", do not create a public wrapper that only forwards a call). `findMenuItem = (menu, id) => requireMenuItem(menu, id)` is an exact alias of `requireMenuItem` (lines 46-50) and adds nothing. Fix: delete `findMenuItem` and use `requireMenuItem` in `catering-notices.mjs`.

- `src/catering/catering-time.mjs:1` (used at `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:4` and `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:11`): Violates `docs/agents/writing.md` Common capabilities (no forwarding-only public wrapper). The module only re-exports `DAY` and `addMinutes` from `src/platform/time.mjs` and hides no complexity; it is a Middle Man. Rule 7.1 lets a feature module import platform modules directly. Fix: import `addMinutes` and `DAY` from `../platform/time.mjs` at the three import sites and delete `catering-time.mjs`.

- `src/catering/catering-pricing.mjs:9-13` (`share`), duplicating `src/billing/totals.mjs:5` (`roundedTax`): Duplicated Code, and a generic mechanism placed in a feature module, against the common design check and `docs/agents/writing.md` Common capabilities. Both compute a basis-point share rounded half up: `share` returns `Math.round((amount * basisPoints) / 1e4)` and `roundedTax` returns `Math.floor((taxable * basisPoints + BASIS / 2) / BASIS)` with `BASIS = 10_000`. For the non-negative amounts used here they produce the same result. The rounding does not depend on billing or catering semantics, so it belongs in a platform module (for example `src/platform/amounts.mjs`, next to `sumOf`). Fix: move the basis-point rounding into the platform module, have `billing/totals.mjs` and `catering-pricing.mjs` both import it, and delete `share`. This keeps one rounding rule to change.

- `src/catering/vendors.mjs:9-12` (`vendorFor`, with `LARGE_ORDER = 30` at line 1) and `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:19-25` (`KITCHENS`): Duplicated Code and Shotgun Surgery. The vendor-routing rule is written twice: `vendorFor` routes halal to `crescent` and headcount above 30 to `banquet`; `KITCHENS` routes halal to `crescent` and `headcount >= 31` to `banquet`, then `deli`. Concrete consequence: the placement path stores `order.vendorId` in `newOrder` (`src/catering/catering-states.mjs`), but `kitchenManifests` ignores that stored value and recomputes the group with `kitchenFor`. A change to `vendorFor` or `LARGE_ORDER` would leave manifests grouped under the old rule, and the literal `31` must be kept in sync with `30` by hand. If `kitchenFor` returns a vendor that `vendorManifests` did not fetch (`menus[vendorId]` is undefined), `requireMenuItem(undefined, ...)` throws a `TypeError`. Fix: group by the persisted `order.vendorId`, delete `KITCHENS` and `kitchenFor`, and rename the groups to vendor naming (`kitchenFor` returns vendor identifiers, which is a mismatched name).

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:137-138` (`deskDeliveries`), duplicating `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:22` (`deliveryWindow`) and `src/catering/kitchen-manifest.mjs:52` (`contains(period, deliveryWindow(order))`): Duplicated Code. `deskDeliveries` rebuilds the delivery window inline (`arrivesFrom = order.deliverAt - CATERING.deliveryLead`, then `arrivesFrom >= day && order.deliverAt <= day + DAY`) instead of reusing `deliveryWindow` and `contains`. The two definitions of "due on this day" must agree, and a change to the window or to `CATERING.deliveryLead` must be made in two places. Fix: `if (order.buildingId === buildingId && contains({startAt: day, endAt: day + DAY}, deliveryWindow(order))) due.push(order);`.

- `src/catering/catering-policy.mjs:8-11` (`prepMinutes` switch), `src/catering/catering-notices.mjs:7` (`SERVING_ORDER`), and `src/catering/menu.mjs:13` (`COURSES`): Repeated Switches and Shotgun Surgery. The set and order of courses is written in three places. Adding a course requires editing all three files; if a course is added only to `COURSES`, `SERVING_ORDER[left.item.course]` becomes `undefined`, the sort comparator returns `NaN`, and `menuLines` silently produces an arbitrary order for the placed, vendor, and confirmed notices. Fix: define each course once in `menu.mjs` (for example as a table with the serving order and prep minutes) and derive the sort order and the prep time from that table.

- `src/catering/catering-statements.mjs:14-15` (`withCanceled`): Speculative Generality. The `{withCanceled = false}` option is never passed by any caller: `vendorStatements` (`src/catering/catering-service.mjs:145`) calls `vendorStatement(delivered, vendorId, period)` with three arguments, and it passes only delivered orders, so the canceled branch of `counted` is dead code. Fix: remove the option and keep `counted` as `deliveredIn(period)`.

- `src/catering/catering-service.mjs:1-151` (module as a whole): Divergent Change. The file mixes order-placement and state-changing commands (`placeOrder`, `addLine`, `postponeOrder`, `cancelOrder`) with read models and reports (`listOrders`, `deskDeliveries`, `vendorStatements`, `memberInvoiceCharges`, `vendorManifests`). The report and manifest functions change for reporting reasons (statement fields, manifest columns, billing charge shape), but they share the module with the placement transaction, which depends on the desk schedule, notifier, and menu feeds. A change to a report therefore edits the same file that owns the placement and notification flow . Fix: move the read-only report and manifest exports into a separate service module in the catering feature (for example `catering-reports-service.mjs`), and keep the order commands in `catering-service.mjs`.
